question: What scriptural texts do Catholics most commonly cite in defense of the doctrine of Purgatory?

choices.A: 2 Maccabees 12:46 (praying for the dead to be freed from sin) and 1 Corinthians 3:15 (saved 'as through fire')
choices.C: Luke 16:19-31 (Lazarus and the rich man) alone
choices.D: The doctrine has no scriptural basis and relies entirely on Tradition

teaching.title: Scripture and Purgatory
teaching.body: The main scriptural pillars for Purgatory: (1) 2 Maccabees 12:46 — Judas Maccabeus makes an atonement offering for fallen soldiers 'so that they might be released from their sin,' which only makes sense if the dead can still be purified. (2) 1 Corinthians 3:12-15 — Paul speaks of a person's work being tested by fire; they may be saved 'but only as through fire.' (3) Matthew 12:32 — Jesus speaks of sins not forgiven 'either in this age or in the age to come,' implying some forgiveness is possible after death. Protestants dispute these readings but acknowledge 2 Maccabees as the clearest witness — which is why they removed it from their canon.
